children: Hong Kong's bourse operator said on Tuesday that HKEX

and the London Metal Exchange have been hit with a new claim from Elliott Associates over cancelled 2022 nickel trades, as the hedge fund renews its legal challenge following the UK courts' dismissal of its earlier case.

Elliott has claimed that the LME, the world's largest and oldest metals exchange, abused its dominant market position by failing to prevent the chaotic nickel trade in which $12 billion worth of contracts were cancelled, HKEX, which owns the LME, said.
HKEX said it has not been served with the claim and that Elliott must first obtain permission from the UK Competition Appeal Tribunal to serve proceedings.
"Any grant of permission may be subject to further challenge by HKEX," the operator said.
Elliott did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Under the new claim, Elliott also alleges that the exchanges failed to identify and manage conflicts of interest and to apply transparent, objective and proportionate trading rules. Any damages would be assessed by the tribunal if Elliott succeeds.
In 2022, the LME halted trading and cancelled the contracts after the metal's prices more than doubled within hours to above $100,000 a metric ton. Elliott then sued the exchange for $456 million.
Elliott's judicial challenge over the LME's handling of the 2022 nickel market crisis ended in 2025 after the UK Supreme Court refused it permission to appeal an October 2024 Court of Appeal ruling.
"Elliott itself now accepts that those actions were lawful as a matter of public law," the LME said in an emailed statement.
"Despite this, Elliott is bringing a new claim in a misguided further attempt to seek damages through an alternative legal route. We consider it to be without merit and will contest it vigorously.”

In March 2025, the LME also settled an enforcement investigation by the UK Financial Conduct Authority, which said large over-the-counter positions were the main driver of the sharp price surge and that the exchange had not been able to see those positions, according to HKEX's 2025 interim report.
However, Britain's financial authority imposed a penalty of £9.2 million ($12.44 million) on the LME at the time.
"HKEX is of the view that the 2026 CAT Claim is without merit and will contest it vigorously," the bourse operator said.
